advances: The exact separated one-breakpoint endpoints of accepted fact `95d6551f9cbc3d06` admit no common middle crossing extension.  The universal extension-cone gate fails strictly in both the \(j\)- and \(k\)-coordinates.  This excludes every compact convex extension, not merely rational polygons or a selected cell allocation, and therefore removes this endpoint survivor before any later exact-cell or crossing-profile test.
author: r108_opposite_middle_extension
proof:
Accepted fact `95d6551f9cbc3d06` verifies the convex endpoint polygons above and gives
\[
M=\frac{1093357}{1000},\qquad
m=\frac{745313}{10000},\qquad
|S|=\frac{1461221}{1600},
\tag{1}
\]
together with
\[
\begin{aligned}
s_j&=\frac{435345209083907707}{589392739124\cdot10000},\\
s_k&=\frac{670981903}{9116250},\\
s_\ell&=\frac{918419314911937}{12463639760000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
It also gives the following counterclockwise vertex list for \(S\):
\[
\begin{gathered}
\left(-\frac{3447}{100},-\frac{19}{100}\right),
\left(-\frac{1381}{40},-\frac38\right),
\left(-\frac{3407}{100},-\frac{159}{200}\right),
\left(-\frac{739}{50},-\frac{43}{40}\right),\\
\left(\frac{323}{20},-\frac{79}{200}\right),
\left(\frac{6259}{200},\frac1{100}\right),
\left(\frac{1603}{50},\frac{59}{200}\right),
\left(\frac{2263}{200},\frac{3417}{200}\right),\\
\left(\frac{1059}{100},\frac{1747}{100}\right),
\left(-\frac{4497}{200},\frac{3351}{200}\right),
\left(-\frac{4777}{200},\frac{667}{40}\right).
\end{gathered}
\tag{3}
\]

The \(j\)-cap clipping in accepted fact `95d6551f9cbc3d06`, and direct exact clipping of (3) by \(x\leq0\) and \(y\leq0\), give
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_j(S)&:=|S\cap\{f_j\leq0\}|
=\frac{2161516250691}{3919640000},\\
c_k(S)&:=|S\cap\{f_k\leq0\}|
=\frac{10601364910761}{20207600000},\\
c_\ell(S)&:=|S\cap\{f_\ell\leq0\}|
=\frac{48004934983}{1092852000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
For an exact audit of the two new clips, the cyclic vertex list of \(S\cap\{x\leq0\}\) is
\[
\begin{gathered}
\left(-\frac{3447}{100},-\frac{19}{100}\right),
\left(-\frac{1381}{40},-\frac38\right),
\left(-\frac{3407}{100},-\frac{159}{200}\right),
\left(-\frac{739}{50},-\frac{43}{40}\right),\\
\left(0,-\frac{463987}{618600}\right),
\left(0,\frac{950414}{55125}\right),
\left(-\frac{4497}{200},\frac{3351}{200}\right),
\left(-\frac{4777}{200},\frac{667}{40}\right),
\end{gathered}
\tag{5}
\]
and the cyclic vertex list of \(S\cap\{y\leq0\}\) is
\[
\begin{gathered}
\left(-\frac{3447}{100},-\frac{19}{100}\right),
\left(-\frac{1381}{40},-\frac38\right),
\left(-\frac{3407}{100},-\frac{159}{200}\right),
\left(-\frac{739}{50},-\frac{43}{40}\right),\\
\left(\frac{323}{20},-\frac{79}{200}\right),
\left(\frac{500921}{16200},0\right),
\left(-\frac{2896627}{84325},0\right).
\end{gathered}
\tag{6}
\]
Each new point in (5)-(6) is obtained by solving one linear edge-cut equation in (3).  The shoelace formula on (5) and (6) gives the last two values in (4).

Apply the abstract gate before any construction.  At the base body \(S\), the common crossing level is
\[
h_S=\frac{2(M+m+|S|)}9=\frac{83246057}{180000}.
\tag{7}
\]
In the index order \((j,k,\ell)\), define
\[
\rho_i=s_i+c_i(S)-h_S.
\]
Equations (1), (2), (4), and (7) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_j&=\frac{4319034448082028329}{26522673260580000},\\
\rho_k&=\frac{60016926994685179}{442122080400000},\\
\rho_\ell&=-\frac{348159026303329207}{100955482056\cdot10000}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Writing \(\Gamma=\rho_j+\rho_k+\rho_\ell\), the first two gate coordinates are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat z_j
&=-\rho_j-\frac23\Gamma
=-\frac{5\rho_j+2\rho_k+2\rho_\ell}{3}\\
&=-\frac{531394949804090915467954709324993}
{4025897096131662344569676700000}<0,\\[1mm]
\widehat z_k
&=-\rho_k-\frac23\Gamma
=-\frac{2\rho_j+5\rho_k+2\rho_\ell}{3}\\
&=-\frac{67569675177567816975642675605573}
{644143535381065975131148272000}<0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

Accepted fact `89563f2f27529ab0`, with its indices \(1,2,3\) identified with \(j,k,\ell\), applies to every compact convex \(K\supseteq S\).  If such a \(K\) satisfied all three crossings, its seven actual added cell areas
\[
z_G=|(K\setminus S)\cap\mathcal C_G|\geq0
\qquad
\bigl(G=j,k,\ell,jk,j\ell,k\ell,jk\ell\bigr)
\]
would satisfy \(\mathsf A z=-9\rho\).  The exact \(j\)-coordinate multiplier from that accepted fact is
\[
w_j=\frac1{27}(5,2,2),
\qquad
w_j^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A
=\left(1,0,0,\frac53,\frac53,\frac23,\frac73\right)\geq0.
\tag{10}
\]
Therefore every actual extension would have to obey
\[
0\leq w_j^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A z
=w_j^{\mathsf T}(-9\rho)
=\widehat z_j.
\tag{11}
\]
This contradicts the strict negative rational value in (9).  The contradiction uses the cell cone only as a proved necessity for every geometric extension \(K\supseteq S\); it does not infer a body from a formal cell allocation.  Hence no compact convex common middle exists at any area.  In particular, none exists in the required radical-free interval \(M-m<\kappa<M+m\), and the additional proper-cap conditions cannot be met.
statement:
Set
\[
f_k(x,y)=x,\qquad f_\ell(x,y)=y,\qquad
f_j(x,y)=-1-x-y
\]
and
\[
p_j=\frac{1566}{25}-x-y,\quad p_k=x,\quad p_\ell=y,
\qquad
q_j=-\frac{1616}{25}-x-y,\quad q_k=x,\quad q_\ell=y.
\]
Let
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\bigg\{&
\left(-\frac1{10},-\frac{49}{100}\right),
\left(\frac{81}{100},-\frac{133}{100}\right),
\left(\frac{6267}{100},\frac3{100}\right),\\
&\left(\frac{1059}{50},\frac{3361}{100}\right),
\left(\frac1{100},-\frac3{25}\right)\bigg\}
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\bigg\{&
\left(-\frac{1379}{20},-\frac{13}{50}\right),
\left(-\frac{3037}{100},-\frac{41}{50}\right),
\left(-\frac2{25},-\frac1{100}\right),\\
&\left(\frac{29}{20},\frac{14}{25}\right),
\left(0,\frac{133}{100}\right),
\left(-\frac{1323}{20},-\frac1{10}\right)\bigg\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Put
\[
M=|A_0|,\qquad m=|A_2|,\qquad S=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2},
\]
and, for \(i=j,k,\ell\), put
\[
s_i=|A_0\cap\{p_i\leq0\}|+|A_2\cap\{q_i\leq0\}|.
\]
There do not exist a rational number \(\kappa\) and a compact two-dimensional rational convex polygon \(K\) such that
\[
M-m<\kappa<M+m,\qquad |K|=\kappa,\qquad S\subseteq K,
\]
and, with
\[
t=\frac{2(M+m+\kappa)}9,
\]
\[
|K\cap\{f_i\leq0\}|=t-s_i
\qquad(i=j,k,\ell).
\]
In fact, no two-dimensional compact convex body \(K\supseteq S\), of any area and without any rationality assumption, satisfies these three crossing equalities.
